title: Default data stage for analysis = subtracted
text: For ALL analysis (Guinier, Kratky, Porod/power-law, P(r), tier-1 ladder passes, form-factor/sasmodels fitting, and curve overlays intended for interpretation), always read curves from the SUBTRACTED folder (stage='subtracted', files ending '_sub.dat') by default. Do NOT analyse averaged (un-subtracted) curves unless the user explicitly names a different stage/folder for that specific request. Exceptions that legitimately use the averaged stage: per-frame acquisition metadata (I0/bstop/transmission/temperature) via plot_metadata, frame-outlier QC via assess_quality, and background-vs-sample contrast checks. If the requested sample has no subtracted counterpart, say so and ask rather than silently falling back to the averaged file.

title: Beamline geometry source of truth
text: The beamline 1-5 knowledge YAML (ssrl_1-5.yml) is OUTDATED and must NOT be used as the source of truth for detector geometry, sample-detector distance, beam centre, or q-range. Always read actual geometry from: (1) the .poni calibration file(s) in the project, and (2) the Reduction app's current configuration. If neither is available for a given session, ask the user before assuming any detector parameter. Do not quote q-ranges, pixel sizes, or SDD values from the YAML without first verifying against the poni/Reduction app.

title: Always verify q-units before any operation
text: Before ANY plotting, analysis, feedback, or numerical statement about a curve, explicitly verify the q-axis units of the loaded .dat file. Units may be Å⁻¹ or nm⁻¹ depending on the reduction configuration; NEVER assume. Check the file header or reduction config for the unit declaration. If uncertain, flag it and ask the user. All internal analysis and reporting must use consistent units — state which unit is in use at the top of every analysis summary. Mixing Å⁻¹ and nm⁻¹ (factor of 10 difference) produces completely wrong Rg, d-spacing, and power-law results.

title: No Bragg peak claims without WAXS confirmation
text: Do NOT report, count, or build any interpretation on putative Bragg peaks found in the SAXS high-q tail (typically q > ~2 nm⁻¹ / 0.2 Å⁻¹) without independent confirmation from the WAXS detector. Reasons: (a) SAXS SNR degrades rapidly at high q and peak-finders will trigger on noise; (b) the q_usable_max boundary itself is noise-limited and wanders run-to-run; (c) a real crystalline reflection must appear at the SAME q in both SAXS and WAXS and must be reproducible across frames. The required check is: overlay the SAXS and WAXS subtracted curves for the same sample and confirm peak positions match. Until that check passes, classify any high-q SAXS feature as 'unconfirmed / likely noise'.
